correctness.rationale: For n>=3 every cycle edge has a uniquely signed lift; a closed n-step word has displacement 0 or ±n. Odd parity excludes 0 for odd n, and the two remaining walks give automorphisms, of which only the identity is idempotent. An idempotent fixes its image pointwise. A proper connected image is an induced path, not a point because adjacent vertices cannot be identified. On an image arc of k edges the complementary arc must go from k to 0 in L=2m−k steps, requiring k<=m. Conversely each strip walk defines exactly one retraction onto the chosen arc. There are 2m arcs, including at k=m; the only arc-set stabilizers are the identity and the endpoint-swapping reflection. The latter acts by w(t)↦k−w(L−t). At an even midpoint it requires height k/2, and at an odd midpoint either orientation of the central edge between (k−1)/2 and (k+1)/2 is admissible. The walk can be freely specified until that midpoint, giving s and integral Burnside counts. The endpoint entry of (I−tA)^(-1) has cofactor t^k and denominator the path continuant. Independently, alternating free-walk images at the two absorbing walls give binomial terms with period k+2; by binomial symmetry the direct-image index can be written m+j(k+2), and the reflected index is m+1+j(k+2). Prepending k up-steps gives a Dyck path whose initial maximal ascent attains the global maximum, allowing later returns. These arguments cover n=3 and n=4 and the endpoint k=m without an exception.
residual_risks: Replay is finite; the induced-arc, wall-reflection and stabilizer arguments supply the all-size conclusions.
